title: No Link Between Mortality and Vessel Diameter in the Congo Basin Forests
content: The spatial patterns of biomass carbon storage in tropical rainforests seems to be primarily driven by mortality rather than tree growth. Mortality can be caused mechanically and hydraulically, covering both failure of sap flow or carbon starvation. In our trait-based ecology research, we focused on one single anatomical trait, the vessel diameter. Mortality data were derived from inventories conducted in the equatorial rainforests of the Congo Basin covering a total period of 11 years. Vessel diameters were obtained from the Inside Wood database, completed with new measurements of reference material and transformed into a 7-level ordinal scale. We sought to determine whether species coexisting within the same tropical forest community exhibit a higher mortality rate when they have larger diameter vessels. We were unable to confirm this link.
